Great questions — looping in Marissa (solutions engineering) and Aditya (sales engineering) to cover the technical details and propose a PoC plan. Quick answers up front: 

- Control plane models:
  * Redwood-hosted control plane (default): minimal infra work on your side, managed telemetry, we offer encrypted audit logs and RBAC. Control-plane traffic is limited to control ports and can be pinned to a region; we offer private peering (VPC Peering/PrivateLink) for control traffic.
  * Private customer-managed control plane: we can deploy a control plane in your VPC or on-prem (customer-managed). This gives you full control of networking and metadata access; telemetry is streamed to your endpoints.

- Air-gap: we support an air-gapped on-prem installation via an offline installer and signed artifact bundle. Updates are provided as offline packages you can pull into an internal artifact repository.

- KMS/HSM: we support integration patterns for customer-managed KMS and HSMs (including PKCS#11 proxies and cloud KMS). We'll need to validate exact HSM model during the deep-dive.

- Performance: we have benchmarked similar models vs hyperscaler endpoints; see attached redwood-private-vpc-compare.pdf. We'll include model-specific numbers for clinical-summarizer-v2 and triage-embed-1 in the deep-dive.

Attachments: network-checklist.xlsx, mutual-action-plan.docx, redwood-private-vpc-compare.pdf

Proposed PoC tests:
1) Private control plane in Acme VPC with peering and restricted egress — validate end-to-end request flow and audit logs.
2) Air-gapped on-prem install (single rack) — validate offline install and model loading.
3) Performance head-to-head: 1k concurrent short-prompt requests and 100 concurrent long-context streaming requests to compare latency/p99 and cost.

Can we get Naomi and a procurement contact confirmed for a 45–60 minute deep-dive next Tue/Wed?

Thanks,
Vanessa

Hi Tom/Team — Marissa from Solutions Engineering here. Adding more technical detail to help your infra team evaluate feasibility. Highlights: 

1) Control plane & data plane separation:
- We support split control/data plane topologies. Control plane can be hosted (Redwood) or deployed into your VPC. Data plane (inference workers) runs in customer-managed subnets in both Dedicated and Private deployment modes.
- For hosted control plane with private peering we recommend: control-plane endpoints over PrivateLink, no public IPs for management interfaces, and strict IAM roles for audit access.

2) Networking checklist & ports (high level):
- Egress rules: allow outbound to Redwood control-plane CIDR for updates if using hosted control plane. For air-gapped installs this is not required.
- Required ports: 443 (control plane TLS), 50051 (gRPC) between control and workers if using internal gRPC; SSH only for maintenance windows.
- CIDR allocation: recommend /24 per worker pool initially.

3) KMS/HSM and secrets management:
- We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM via PKCS#11. For air-gapped installs we provide a signed key-rotation tool that you can run against your HSM.

4) Audit & compliance:
- Audit logs (requests, model versions, rollouts) can be streamed to your SIEM (Splunk/Elastic) or stored in customer S3 with server-side encryption. Retention controls are configurable.

5) PoC test harness suggestions:
- Load: 1k concurrent short requests (avg 50 tokens), 100 concurrent long-streaming sessions (avg 1k tokens)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens.
- Comparison: run identical workload against AWS Bedrock endpoint and Redwood Private cluster during the same window to control for network variance.

I'll be happy to walk through the network checklist with Naomi on the call. I've attached the network-checklist.xlsx and mutual-action-plan.docx that Vanessa included — they include fields for CIDRs, firewall rules, and procurement milestones.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
